overlayLegend.H: hairline guide (default fraction of the first head-unit band)
overlayLegend.S: shoulder line guide (default fraction, adjust to observed pose)
overlayLegend.P: hip line guide (default fraction, adjust to observed pose)

proportions.notes: torso = neck-base->hip-joint trunk segment in HU (the quantity new_sculpt_spec._hu_ratio consumes); crownToHip is the reconstruction.md definition. shoulderWidth = shoulder joint-to-joint (outer boxy jacket ~1.25 HU). hipWidth = 0.8 HU (pants outer at hip y=370 is 129px = 0.78 HU). Figure = 3.5 skull-HU incl. hair tuft, 2.85 HU if the hair mass is counted as head.

pose.type: A-pose; bind pose == reference pose (angles baked into attachment endpoints, jointAngles left at identity to avoid double application)
pose.stance: symmetric, weight centred, feet planted shoulder-width apart, toes slightly outward

faceLandmarks.notes: Normalized to the head box (skull top est. y=55 -> chin y=221). No eyes, nose or ears are depicted: eyeLine is the goggle-lens centre line (the lens occupies the eye region); eyeSpacing/noseBase/ear values are not applicable (null), not unmeasured. hairline = lower edge of the slime fringe where it meets the goggle frame.

features: goggles cover the eye region (single wide lens)
no nose, no ears, no visible eyes
anatomy.styleAxis: chibi/stylized (between chibi 2-3 HU and stylized 5-6 HU)
anatomy.measurementSource: reference/front.png 400x615, PIL row/column scans of the foreground mask (bg rgb 244,243,239); ground y=600, figure top (hair tuft) y=16
anatomy.landmarkTooling: extract_landmarks.py (stdlib overlay+scaffold) ran; MediaPipe face/pose landmarks are not applicable to an eyeless/noseless stylized slime face behind goggles, so values were measured manually from pixels.

authoringInstruction: Open overlayImage and read the reference against its head-unit ticks, thirds grid, face-line guides, shoulder/hip lines, and center axis. Replace every null/placeholder value in anatomy with normalized coordinates or joint angles actually observed; the drawn guide lines are generic starting positions, not measurements.
